q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

Let me work through this systematically.

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is 2026-08-13. Q2 FY2027 would typically end in July 2026 (NVIDIA's fiscal year runs August-July). The earnings release already occurred on May 20, 2026 (per the research), meaning the guidance has already been provided. Time to resolution: essentially 0 days — this is a resolved question with publicly available information.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The research explicitly states that NVIDIA provided forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 in its Q1 FY2027 earnings release on May 20, 2026. The guidance is:

**$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%**

This translates to a range of:
- Low: $91.0B × 0.98 = $89.18B
- High: $91.0B × 1.02 = $92.82B

The midpoint is $91.0 billion.

Since the guidance has already been publicly announced by NVIDIA in an official SEC filing and press release, this is the company's official forward guidance for Q2 FY2027. The most likely outcome is that the actual figure falls within the ±2% band that NVIDIA specified.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Weaker than expected demand in data centers (primary revenue driver)
- Supply chain disruptions affecting delivery schedules
- Geopolitical restrictions beyond China (though China restrictions already baked into guidance)
- Competitive pressure from AMD or other competitors capturing market share
- Macro recession reducing customer capex spending

However, NVIDIA's guidance already explicitly excludes China data center revenue, providing a cushion for uncertainty.

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Better than expected AI demand acceleration
- Higher ASPs (average selling prices) for new product generations
- Enterprise customers pulling forward orders before potential tariffs or restrictions
- Stronger than expected OEM/edge/automotive revenue
- Upside surprises in software/services revenue

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides the actual guidance: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**. This is not a prediction — it is NVIDIA's stated official guidance from their May 20, 2026 earnings call, filed with the SEC. This is the ground truth for this question.

The guidance of $91.0B ± 2% ($89.18B to $92.82B) falls **below** the provided forecast range which starts at 99.5B. This is surprising and suggests either:
1. The range given is an error or refers to a different period
2. The question is asking for something beyond the midpoint guidance (e.g., upside scenarios)
3. There's been subsequent guidance revision

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA has already provided forward guidance for its Q2 FY2027 revenue in its Q1 FY2027 earnings release on May 20, 2026. The company expects revenue for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 to be **$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%** [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/). This figure is well above the average quarterly revenue estimate of $86.84 billion, according to LSEG [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).

NVIDIA's guidance explicitly states that it is **not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China** in this outlook [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/). The company also provided gross margin expectations of 74.9% (GAAP) and 75.0% (non-GAAP), plus or minus 50 basis points, and operating expenses of approximately $8.5 billion (GAAP) and $8.3 billion (non-GAAP) [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/).
